_comment: Hand-curated layer of docs/capabilities.json (capability-config.md §2 p.3). The emitter (stapel_notifications/_capabilities.py) merges this over the derived axes; an axis present in conf.py DEFAULTS but missing here (or vice versa) is a loud emission error. Keep business_label/summary in business language — they surface in CTO conversations, not in code. Since the usage-surface wave the file also carries surface_roots + one intent line per selected symbol (stapel_tools.surface): the routing readers, the dispatch entry point and every packaged email template, so "is there already a letter/mechanism for X" has a machine-readable answer. A symbol a root selects and this map does not explain is a loud emission error too.
provides: Multi-channel user notifications: routes typed notification requests to email, SMS and push with per-user preferences and language, branded email templates, device push-token management and an in-app notification feed; delivery is logged per channel with idempotency.

requires.reason: comm bus (notification.requested input, translate.resolve calls), JWT authentication, GDPR provider registry, AppSettings config layer
source of the user-contact sync (email/phone projections) and the user.deleted / user.deletion_initiated events this module consumes; decoupled via the comm bus
source of the notification-preferences and language sync (profile-changed events consumed into UserNotificationSettings); decoupled via the comm bus
notification texts are localized through the translate.resolve comm Function with lazy caching; without it the built-in English defaults are used

extension_points.name: TYPES
extension_points.summary: Register new notification types (channels + group + template) or override built-ins entirely from settings — merged over the packaged routing catalog, no fork.

extension_points.name: EMAIL_TEMPLATES
extension_points.summary: Remap any notification type to a host-project email template; merged over the packaged per-type template map.

extension_points.name: channel_providers
extension_points.summary: The EMAIL/SMS/PUSH provider settings accept any dotted path to a class with the matching send() signature — add SendGrid, Postmark, APNs etc. as host-project classes, no fork.

extension_points.name: template_overrides
extension_points.summary: Packaged email templates live under a namespaced path and follow standard Django template-loader precedence; eject_notification_templates copies them into the host project for structural edits, and LOGO_URL/BRAND_*/COMPANY_* settings rebrand every email without touching a template.

extension_points.name: serializer_seams
extension_points.summary: Every view declares request/response serializer seams (SerializerSeamMixin) — subclass the view, override the attribute, remount the URL.

EMAIL_PROVIDER.summary: Which service sends the emails: Resend, SMTP, Mailgun, or any custom provider class supplied by the host project. Defaults to 'unconfigured', which refuses to send until a backend is chosen; 'mock' (log only, no delivery) must be asked for by name.

SMS_PROVIDER.summary: Which service sends the text messages: GatewayAPI, Twilio, or any custom provider class supplied by the host project. Defaults to 'unconfigured', which refuses to send until a backend is chosen; 'mock' (log only, no delivery) must be asked for by name.

PUSH_PROVIDER.summary: Which service delivers mobile/web push: Firebase Cloud Messaging (default), 'mock' for log-only development, 'unconfigured' to close the channel outright, or any custom provider class supplied by the host project.

process_notification.intent: THE dispatch entry point: give it a notification_type plus variables and it resolves the recipient's language, their contacts and preferences, the translations, the branded template and every configured channel, then writes one NotificationLog row per channel with event_id idempotency. Call it in-process (it is what the notification.requested consumer calls); across a service boundary publish through stapel_core.notifications.request_notification instead, which lands here. Do not assemble an email and a log row yourself — the language chain alone (saved preference → caller's language → remembered → the request's active language → project default) is four fallbacks deep, and every level of it was added because a product shipped English OTP codes to a non-English locale.

default_language.intent: The project's fallback language — STAPEL_LANGUAGE["DEFAULT"], then Django's LANGUAGE_CODE — and never a hardcoded "en": a service built for a non-English market gets every English string as a defect. A module-local alias of stapel_core.language.default_language; outside this package reach for the core one directly.

get_routing.intent: The effective routing entry ({channels, group, template}) of a type, with STAPEL_NOTIFICATIONS["TYPES"] merged over the packaged catalog — the primitive the other readers sit on. Prefer get_channels/get_group/get_email_template when the question is narrower, and never merge the settings dict over routing.NOTIFICATION_ROUTING by hand: an override replaces a built-in wholesale, which a naive dict update gets wrong.

registered_types.intent: Every notification type this deployment knows, built-ins plus the host's TYPES registrations — ask it before requesting a type you are not sure exists, because an unregistered type without content_html/content_text is dropped with a logged error rather than delivered. `manage.py check_notifications` is the CI-time form of the same question over literal call sites.

get_channels.intent: The channels a type is routed to after host overrides — read this rather than the settings dict when a caller has to know whether a type reaches SMS or push at all (an empty list means the type is unregistered).

get_group.intent: The preference group of a type, from a CLOSED vocabulary (routing.VALID_GROUPS): "auth" is mandatory and carries no unsubscribe, "messages" and "system" are user-mutable per channel and are the only groups whose mail may carry one. An unknown group is notifications.E001 at boot — the group also names the preference field, so mail under a misspelled group is mail nobody can switch off. This is the value that decides whether a user may switch the notification off, so read it before a UI promises an opt-out — and before classifying a new type, because putting a marketing message in the auth group is how a deployment loses its List-Unsubscribe compliance.

get_email_template.intent: The email template a type actually renders with, resolving the whole precedence chain (the routing entry's "template" key → the EMAIL_TEMPLATES override → the packaged default). Reach for it instead of hardcoding a template path, which silently ignores the host's remap.

notifications/email/_base.html.intent: The shared email shell every packaged letter extends: header/logo, body slot, footer, and the logo_url/brand_*/company_* variables process_notification threads into every render. A host template for a new type should extend this and fill the `content` block (plus `preheader`/`footer`/`head_extra` as needed) rather than start from a blank HTML document — that is what makes a product's own letter look like the rest of the mail the deployment sends, and what makes the branding settings apply to it for free.

notifications/email/_footer_unsubscribe..intent: The unsubscribe / manage-preferences footer that _base.html switches to whenever `unsubscribe_url` is present — which routing.unsubscribe_allowed grants only to a type in an allowlisted group (`messages`, `system`) that is neither transactional nor security-class. Do not write an unsubscribe line into a custom template by hand: the URL, its signed token and the matching one-click List-Unsubscribe headers are produced together by process_notification, and a hand-written link stops working the moment the token scheme moves.

notifications/email/_raw_content.html.intent: The raw-content wrapper that puts a caller-supplied content_html/content_text inside the brand layout — what makes the request_notification(..., content_html=...) escape hatch possible for a type that is deliberately not registered. Reach for the escape hatch, not for this template directly.

notifications/email/otp_code.html.intent: The one-time-code letter — notification_type `otp_code`, auth group (mandatory, no unsubscribe), routed to email and SMS. Request the type instead of composing a verification-code mail: the code formatting, the branding and the language resolution are already handled.

notifications/email/magic_link_login.htm.intent: The passwordless sign-in link letter — notification_type `magic_link_login`, auth group, email only.

notifications/email/auth_change.html.intent: One template serving the whole authenticator-change sequence — notification_types `auth_change_requested`, `auth_change_reminder`, `auth_change_urgent` and `auth_change_completed` (auth group; email, SMS and push). Four stages of a single flow share it, so one EMAIL_TEMPLATES remap re-skins all of them.

notifications/email/new_device_login.htm.intent: The "new sign-in to your account" security notice — notification_type `new_device_login`, auth group, email only: the letter to send when a session appears from a device the account has not used before.

notifications/email/suspicious_login.htm.intent: The "suspicious sign-in detected" security notice — notification_type `suspicious_login`, auth group, email only. The sharper sibling of new_device_login, for a sign-in the risk logic actually distrusts.

notifications/email/all_sessions_revoked.intent: The "all sessions have been revoked" notice — notification_type `all_sessions_revoked`, auth group, email only. Send it after a global logout so an owner who did not trigger it finds out.

notifications/email/gdpr_export_ready.ht.intent: "Your data export is ready" — notification_type `gdpr.export_ready`, auth group, email only: the letter a subject-access export has to end with.

notifications/email/gdpr_inactivity_warn.intent: "Your account will be closed in N days" — notification_type `gdpr.inactivity_warning`, auth group, email only: the warning a retention-driven closure owes the account before it happens.

notifications/email/gdpr_inactivity_clos.intent: "Your account has been closed" — notification_type `gdpr.inactivity_closed`, auth group, email only: the terminal notice of a retention closure.

notifications/email/new_message.html.intent: The user-to-user message letter — notification_type `new_message`, messages group (the user can switch it off per channel), routed to push first and email second.

notifications/email/report_reviewed.html.intent: "Your report has been reviewed" — notification_type `report_reviewed`, system group, push and email: the moderation-outcome letter for the person who reported.

notifications/email/listing_expiring.htm.intent: "Your listing is expiring" — notification_type `listing_expiring`, system group, push and email: the marketplace lifecycle reminder.

notifications/email/listing_blocked.html.intent: "Your listing has been blocked" — notification_type `listing_blocked`, system group, push and email: the moderation-block notice for the owner.

notifications/email/workspace_invitation.intent: The workspace invitation letter for an invitee who already has an account — notification_type `workspace.invitation`, system group, email only. stapel-workspaces requests it from create_invitation; nothing else should be minting invitation mail, because the single-use token and its TTL belong to that flow.

The invitation letter for a recipient with no account yet — notification_type `workspace.invitation.new_user`. Its own type rather than an override of `workspace.invitation`, because the link both creates the account and joins the workspace and the copy has to say so.

The re-delivery of a pending invitation — notification_type `workspace.invitation.reminder`. An admin resend rotates the token and restarts the TTL, so this is "you are being reminded, here is a fresh link", a different message from the original invitation rather than a repeat of it.

The receipt for the person who refused an invitation — notification_type `workspace.invitation.decline_confirmed`, system group, transactional. Declining rests on the token and creates no account, so the letter carries no link and its whole job is to say the invitation is closed and that nothing was created in order to close it.

The answer to the person who sent an invitation — notification_type `workspace.invitation.declined`, system group, transactional. It names the address the inviter themselves typed, the workspace and the outcome, and nothing else about whoever declined.

notifications/email/workspace_provisione.intent: "Your account is ready" for a member an organization provisioned directly — notification_type `workspace.provisioned_account`, auth group: credentials mail is mandatory and carries no unsubscribe, like every other account-credential letter here.

notifications/email/workspace_mfa_suspen.intent: "Access suspended — two-factor authentication required" — notification_type `workspace.mfa_suspension`, auth group: sent when a workspace's require_mfa sweep suspends a member who has not enrolled.

notifications/email/workspace_mfa_restor.intent: "Access restored" — notification_type `workspace.mfa_restored`, auth group: the counterpart sent when the member enrols or the policy is lifted.

notifications/email/workspace_member_pas.intent: "Your password was reset" — notification_type `workspace.member_password_reset`, auth group. It names the workspace and the admin who did it and never carries the new password: a reset performed by somebody other than the account's owner is indistinguishable from a takeover until the owner is told, which is why this one is mandatory.

is_transactional.intent: True when a type is a one-to-one message triggered by a named person (a workspace invitation) rather than bulk mail. Such a letter carries no unsubscribe affordance at all: RFC 8058 one-click is machine-actionable and this library's token is minted per (user, GROUP, channel), so one automated POST on a personal invitation opts the recipient out of every system email forever. Ask this instead of testing group != "auth" when you are deciding whether an opt-out belongs on a message.

is_security.intent: True when a type is account-security / authentication class — either by living in the `auth` group or by carrying the explicit `"security": True` routing key. The flag exists for the security letter that must stay switch-off-able and therefore cannot live in `auth` ("a new device signed in"): it removes the unsubscribe affordance without touching the group, so the recipient keeps their preference and never gets a one-click opt-out from security mail.

unsubscribe_allowed.intent: THE single decision behind both the unsubscribe footer and the List-Unsubscribe / List-Unsubscribe-Post: One-Click headers, taken over a routing ENTRY (so the raw-content escape hatch, which synthesises one for an unregistered type, is judged by the same rule). It is an allowlist — group in routing.UNSUBSCRIBABLE_GROUPS, not transactional, not security-class — because the predicate it replaced was `group != "auth"`, under which a typo, a missing group key or a settings override that replaced a built-in auth entry wholesale put a machine-actionable opt-out from all security mail on a passcode.

may_carry_unsubscribe.intent: `unsubscribe_allowed` asked by type name — the reader to call from host code or a UI before promising an opt-out on a given notification type. Never re-derive the answer from get_group(): the group is only one of the three inputs, and reimplementing the rule is how the two copies drift.
